- When sentiment is high (≥0.53) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.27) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–2%.
- Model consistently overpredicts in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day windows after strong moves; model fails to reflect this; apply a smoothing filter or lagged adjustment.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model delays correction; anticipate a 1–2 day lag in downward adjustment.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to overestimate; apply a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment remains stable or declines.
